text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Bulgaria's foreign debt payments in 1997 total $992.2 million, central bank figures show. Bulgaria has to pay $336.5 million to foreign creditors in the first quarter, of which $135.1 million were transferred as Brady bond coupon payment at the end of January. @

-- An International Monetary Fund mission could be expected in Bulgaria as soon as a caretaker cabinet is appointed by the president, Bulgaria's representative to the IMF Petar Botusharov told a private radio station.
-- Bulgaria's Socialist leader Georgi Parvanov said in the Black Sea city of Bourgas he was ready to resign as a party chairman.

-- The ecological party within the opposition Union of Democratic Forces (UDF) suggested that Bulgaria's exiled King Simeon lead a cabinet formed by the next parliament after election in April, UDF deputy Evgeni Mihailov said.
-- Bulgaria's montly inflation for January is expected at around 50 percent, National Statistics Institute's estimates show.

-- The Bulgarian Socialist Party (BSP) is expected to win at least 20 percent of the vote at the general elections in April, a senior BSP official said, rejecting opinion polls that the party would get only eight percent.
-- If parliamentary elections were held today the opposition coalition could win up to two thirds of the seats in the parliament, the MBMD polling agency said.
